**Meridian Tidal Pilot - Final Operations Review Summary**

The sole major equipment failure was Turbine T-4 taking offline on 14 March 2025 after its bearing seal corroded through, allowing seawater into the nacelle; root cause was traced to corrosion of the bearing seal housing. Over the full 24-month period the pilot delivered 18.7 GWh to the grid, 6% below the original forecast of 19.9 GWh.

The project finished at EUR 41.25 million against an approved budget of EUR 36.7 million, an overrun of EUR 4.55 million (12.4%), driven mainly by the T-4 repair campaign.

On the environmental front, an independent fish-monitoring programme found no statistically significant change in fish migration counts before and after installation (p = 0.41), indicating negligible marine life impact.

Lead engineer Dr. Ines Marchetti recommended replacing the titanium fastener set with duplex stainless steel on all remaining nacelles to prevent recurrence; the steering group accepted this recommendation in principle.

Final Decision: the steering group approved Phase 2 for Q3 2026, contingent on a completed bearing seal redesign and a successful dry-dock endurance test.
